Primary immunodeficiency with hypogammaglobulinemia; intellectual disability in 7/7 supports neurologic involvement. Recurrent respiratory infections alone do not establish lung damage.

Juvenile parkinsonian-pyramidal neurodegenerative syndrome.

Chlamydia trachomatis infection umbrella; ocular, respiratory and urinary sites vary across subtypes and do not apply to most patients across the group.

Reflex epilepsy triggered by reading; jaw myoclonus and visual symptoms arise from seizure activity rather than separate muscle or eye disease.
Anti-MOG-mediated inflammatory optic neuropathy; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis, and this concept specifies isolated optic neuritis.
FGF23 excess defines a metabolic bone disorder with osteomalacia and renal phosphate wasting in 80-99%; renal involvement is functional. Nephrocalcinosis may be treatment-related.

Familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with myocardial dysfunction and frequent heart failure.
Primary skeletal muscular dystrophy. Reduced FVC in 13/20 reflects respiratory muscle weakness without documented intrinsic lung disease; cardiomyopathy occurs in only 2/23.
Cutaneous infestation by trombiculid mite larvae; transmission of scrub typhus represents a separate infection.
